newsitem.title: USA: Chevron posts record operating earnings.
newsitem.headline: Chevron posts record operating earnings.

text.p: Chevron Corp reported record operating earnings of $837 million in the second quarter on Wednesday, despite a drop in operating sales to $9.95 billion from $10.51 billion amidst lower oil and product prices.

While the company's operating income for the quarter increased 20 percent over last year's $700 million, Chevron's net income dropped to $823 million, or $1.26 a share, compared with a net of $872 million, or $1.34 a share, the year before.
Chevron's net still beat a $1.10-a-share First Call consensus forecast of 24 analysts by $0.16 a share.
"We had another excellent quarter. All our business units turned in strong performances, both financially and operationally," said chief executive Ken Derr in a statement.

Chevron said it took $66 million in charges to pay for its employee stock option program, while it posted $52 million in gains from assets sales and other items in the second quarter. The net-charge totaled $14 million, compared with a net-gain of $172 million in the quarter last year when the company sold its refinery interests in Japan.
Derr said Chevron's worldwide upstream earnings increased on higher production volumes and lower income tax expense in certain countries.

He added downstream operating results also surpassed last year's second quarter, benefiting from lower crude oil prices, lower operating expenses and higher sales., while chemicals earnings improved on lower feedstock costs and stronger prices for some of the company's major products.
"Chevron's return on capital, excluding special items, was 14.0 percent for the 12 months ended June 30 997, compared with 12.8 percent for the year 1996," Derr said.

The company said its ongoing operating expense declined $0.86 to $5.42 per barrel for the quarter, reflecting both lower total expenses and higher production and sales. International liquids production increased 46,000 barrels per day to 734,000 barrels, up seven percent increase over lats year's second quarter.

U.S. exploration and production net earnings declined to $182 million from $194 million in the 1996. The company took a $11 million charge related to the stock option plan in the quarter. The 1996 quarter included a charge of $9 million for environmental remediation.

Average crude oil realizations for the second quarter of $16.86 per barrel were $1.43 lower than last year, while average natural gas prices declined $0.11 per thousand cubic feet to $1.95. The company said lower operating and exploration expenses mitigated the effect of lower oil and gas prices.
Total U.S. oil production decreased to 340,000 barrels per day (bpd) from 342,000 bpd, while natural gas production increased to 1.90 billion cubic feet per day from 1.83 billion.

The company posted $357 million in net earnings on its International exploration and production, up 37 percent from $260 million in 1996. Excluding special items, earnings increased 12 percent to $298 million from $267 million last year.

Chevron's international oil production rose seven percent to 734,000 bpd, with most of the increase coming from the Republic of Congo and the company's TCO affiliate in Kazakstan. Net natural gas production declined to 543 million from 578 million cubic feet per day, principally due to lower production in Australia.
Chevron said foreign currency effects increased the division's earnings $12 million in the quarter, compared with zero in 1996.

The company's U.S. refining and marketing net earnings totaled $182 million in the quarter, compared with $183 million last year. Excluding special charges, earnings increased 12 percent to $217 million from $194 million last year.
Chevron attributed the rise to lower crude oil feedstock costs, lower operating expenses and higher sales. It added refined product sales were up almost six percent to 1.19 million bpd.

Chevron's international refining and marketing net earnings totaled $92 million for the quarter, compared with $302 million last year, when the company gained $260 million from selling refinery interests in Japan. Operating earnings of $95 million more than doubled over 1996's operating earnings of $42 million.

The company attributed the rise to higher sales margins in the United Kingdom and in its affiliate Caltex's Asia-Pacific areas. It also noted a $24 million favorable swing in foreign currency effects, almost all related to Caltex operations.

Chevron's chemical division posted $77 million in net earnings in the quarter, compared with $51 million in 1996. Operating income jumped 28 percent to $86 million from $67 million last year because of lower feedstock costs and price improvements for some of the unit's major products, the company said.
The company said its total capital and exploratory expenditures, including affiliates, totaled $1.30 billion in the quarter, compared with $1.16 billion in 1996.
Chevron sold its five-percent interest in the Tengiz oil field to Lukarco, a joint venture of Arco and Russia's LUKoil for a $32 million gain in the quarter.

In addition, it started oil production from Area C, offshore Angola; successfully bid with partners to operate the LL-652 oil field in Venezuela's Lake Maracaibo for 20 years; and signed a production-sharing contract with China National Petroleum Corp to explore for oil in the Shengli Field Complex, about 200 miles southeast of Beijing.
Chevron's stock opened at a 52-week high of 78 Wednesday morning, but had dropped to 77-3/16 by noon, down 7/16.
